claim: Recent transcriptional profiling technologies are uncovering previously-undefined cell populations and molecular markers at an unprecedented pace.
source: Recent transcriptional profiling technologies are uncovering previously-undefined cell populations and molecular markers at an unprecedented pace.
evidence: This is a general statement about the field that represents established scientific consensus.

claim: A complementary method to isolate and sequence specific cell populations from heterogeneous tissue remains challenging.
source: While single cell RNA (scRNA) sequencing is an attractive approach for unbiased transcriptional profiling of all cell types, a complementary method to isolate and sequence specific cell populations from heterogeneous tissue remains challenging.
evidence: This statement reflects the current state of the field and the motivation for developing Probe-Seq.

claim: Probe-Seq allows deep transcriptional profiling of specific cell types isolated using RNA as the defining feature.
source: Here, we developed Probe-Seq, which allows deep transcriptional profiling of specific cell types isolated using RNA as the defining feature.
evidence: This is the main claim of the paper, supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: Dissociated cells are labeled using fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) for RNA, and then isolated by fluorescent activated cell sorting (FACS).
source: Dissociated cells are labeled using fluorescent in situ hybridization (FISH) for RNA, and then isolated by fluorescent activated cell sorting (FACS).
evidence: This describes the methodological approach of Probe-Seq, which is demonstrated throughout the experimental sections.

claim: Probe-Seq was used to purify and profile specific cell types from mouse, human, and chick retinas, as well as from Drosophila midguts.
source: We used Probe-Seq to purify and profile specific cell types from mouse, human, and chick retinas, as well as from Drosophila midguts.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data presented in multiple figures throughout the manuscript.

claim: Probe-Seq is compatible with frozen nuclei, making cell types within archival tissue immediately accessible.
source: Probe-Seq is compatible with frozen nuclei, making cell types within archival tissue immediately accessible.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments on frozen human and mouse retinas described in the manuscript.

claim: Probe-Seq can be multiplexed, allowing combinations of markers to be used to create specificity.
source: As it can be multiplexed, combinations of markers can be used to create specificity.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experiments showing iterative labeling and sorting with multiple gene-specific probe sets.

claim: Multiplexing allows for the isolation of multiple cell types from one cell preparation.
source: Multiplexing also allows for the isolation of multiple cell types from one cell preparation.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the iterative Probe-Seq experiments shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Probe-Seq should enable RNA profiling of specific cell types from any organism.
source: Probe-Seq should enable RNA profiling of specific cell types from any organism.
evidence: This is supported by successful application to multiple organisms (mouse, human, chick, Drosophila) and represents an inference from the data.

claim: The retina contains seven major cell classes: rods, cones, bipolar cells (BC), amacrine cells (AC), horizontal cells (HC), Müller glia (MG), and retinal ganglion cells (RGC).
source: For example, the retina, a thin sheet of neural tissue in the eye that processes and transmits visual information to the brain, contains seven major cell classes – rods, cones, bipolar cells (BC), amacrine cells (AC), horizontal cells (HC), Müller glia (MG), and retinal ganglion cells (RGC), first defined primarily using morphology (Sanes and Zipursky, 2010; Vlasits et al., 2019).
evidence: This is established knowledge in the field, supported by citations.

claim: scRNA profiling technologies have led to the appreciation of many subtypes of retinal cell classes, bringing the total number of retinal cell types close to 100.
source: More recently, scRNA profiling technologies have led to the appreciation of many subtypes of these major cell classes, bringing the total number of retinal cell types close to 100 (Macosko et al., 2015; Rheaume et al., 2018; Shekhar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to published scRNA sequencing studies.

claim: Bulk RNA sequencing of whole tissues can be done at great depth, but does not capture the diversity of individual transcriptomes and often fails to reflect signatures of rare cell types.
source: Bulk RNA sequencing of whole tissues can be done at great depth, but does not capture the diversity of individual transcriptomes and often fails to reflect signatures of rare cell types.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the limitations of bulk RNA sequencing.

claim: Bulk sequencing of specific cell types is limited by the availability of cell type-specific promoters, enhancers, dyes, or antigens for their isolation.
source: Currently, bulk sequencing of specific cell types is limited by the availability of cell type-specific promoters, enhancers, dyes, or antigens for their isolation (Arlotta et al., 2005; Matsuda and Cepko, 2007; Molyneaux et al., 2015; Siegert et al., 2012; Telley et al., 2016; Xu et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work and represents a known limitation in the field.

claim: Bulk RNA sequencing has been limited primarily to select cell types in genetically-tractable organisms.
source: This has limited bulk RNA sequencing primarily to select cell types in genetically-tractable organisms.
evidence: This is an inference based on the limitations described in the previous sentence and general knowledge of the field.

claim: Single cell and single nucleus RNA sequencing methods have allowed for the recording of transcriptional states of many individual cells simultaneously.
source: Single cell and single nucleus RNA sequencing methods have allowed for the recording of transcriptional states of many individual cells simultaneously (Macosko et al., 2015; Shekhar et al., 2016; Jaitin et al., 2014; Klein et al., 2015; Picelli et al., 2013; Shalek et al., 2013).
evidence: This is established knowledge supported by multiple citations.

claim: Capturing deep profiles of specific cell populations in bulk can be sufficient or preferable for many experiments, for example when the goal is to understand the results of perturbations.
source: Despite the undeniable appeal of scRNA sequencing, capturing deep profiles of specific cell populations in bulk can be sufficient or preferable for many experiments, for example when the goal is to understand the results of perturbations.
evidence: This represents a reasoning about experimental design and the motivation for developing Probe-Seq.

claim: Antibodies have been used to enable FACS-based isolation for transcriptional profiling of specific cell populations.
source: We and others have used antibodies to enable FACS-based isolation for transcriptional profiling of specific cell populations (Molyneaux et al., 2015; Amamoto et al., 2019; Hrvatin et al., 2014; Pan et al., 2011; Pechhold et al., 2009; Yamada et al., 2010a).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous work including the authors' own studies.

claim: Antibodies are frequently unavailable for a specific cell type.
source: However, antibodies are frequently unavailable for a specific cell type.
evidence: This represents a known limitation in the field and motivation for developing alternative methods.

claim: Marker proteins in certain cell types, such as neurons, are often localized to processes that are lost during tissue dissociation.
source: Furthermore, marker proteins in certain cell types, such as neurons, are often localized to processes that are lost during tissue dissociation.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the challenges of working with neuronal tissue.

claim: Probe-Seq uses a FISH method based upon Serial Amplification By Exchange Reaction (SABER).
source: This led us to develop Probe-Seq, which uses a FISH method based upon a new probe design, Serial Amplification By Exchange Reaction (SABER) (Kishi et al., 2019).
evidence: This describes the methodological basis of Probe-Seq, with citation to the SABER method.

claim: Specific cells cultured in vitro have been successfully labeled by FISH for isolation using FACS, but this method had not yet been tested for use in tissue.
source: Although specific cells cultured in vitro have been successfully labeled by FISH for isolation using FACS, this method had not yet been tested for use in tissue (Klemm et al., 2014; Maeda et al., 2016; Yamada et al., 2010b).
evidence: This is supported by citations and establishes the novelty of applying FISH-based FACS to tissue samples.

claim: Probe-Seq was used to isolate rare bipolar cells from the mouse retina.
source: We used Probe-Seq to isolate rare bipolar cells from the mouse retina, cell types that were previously defined using scRNA sequencing (Shekhar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 1 and related text.

claim: Probe sets for multiple genes can be hybridized at once, allowing isolation of multiple cell types simultaneously.
source: We demonstrate that probe sets for multiple genes can be hybridized at once, allowing isolation of multiple cell types simultaneously.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data showing multiplexed labeling.

claim: The fluorescent oligos used to detect the probe sets can be quickly hybridized and then stripped.
source: Moreover, the fluorescent oligos used to detect the probe sets can be quickly hybridized and then stripped.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the iterative Probe-Seq experiments shown in Figure 1i.

claim: Stripping and re-labeling enables isolation of an indefinite number of cell types from one sample by serial sorting and re-labeling.
source: This enables isolation of an indefinite number of cell types from one sample by serial sorting and re-labeling.
evidence: This is an inference based on the demonstrated ability to strip and re-label fluorescent oligos.

claim: Probe-Seq was extended to specific bipolar cell subtypes in frozen archival human retina by labeling nuclear RNA.
source: We extended Probe-Seq to specific bipolar cell subtypes in frozen archival human retina by labeling nuclear RNA.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: Probe-Seq was used to profile intestinal stem cells from the Drosophila gut.
source: To further test the utility of Probe-Seq in non-vertebrate animals and non-CNS tissues, we profiled intestinal stem cells from the Drosophila gut.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 3.

claim: The transcriptional profiles of isolated populations closely matched those obtained by scRNA sequencing.
source: In each of these experiments, the transcriptional profiles of isolated populations closely matched those obtained by scRNA sequencing, and in most cases, the number of genes detected exceeded 10,000.
evidence: This is supported by correlation analyses and gene set enrichment analyses throughout the manuscript.

claim: In most cases, the number of genes detected exceeded 10,000.
source: In each of these experiments, the transcriptional profiles of isolated populations closely matched those obtained by scRNA sequencing, and in most cases, the number of genes detected exceeded 10,000.
evidence: This is supported by the RNA-seq data presented throughout the manuscript.

claim: Probe-Seq was used on the chick retina to determine the transcriptional profile of a subset of developing retinal cells that give rise to the chick high acuity area.
source: Finally, we used Probe-Seq on the chick retina, an organism that is difficult to genetically manipulate, to determine the transcriptional profile of a subset of developing retinal cells that give rise to the chick high acuity area.
evidence: This is demonstrated by experimental data in Figure 4.

claim: Probe-Seq is a method that enables deep transcriptional profiling of specific cell types in heterogeneous tissue from potentially any organism.
source: Taken together, Probe-Seq is a method that enables deep transcriptional profiling of specific cell types in heterogeneous tissue from potentially any organism.
evidence: This is the main conclusion of the paper, supported by successful application to multiple organisms and tissue types.

claim: SABER-FISH uses OligoMiner to design 20–40 nt oligonucleotides that are complementary to the RNA species of interest and are optimized for minimal off-target binding.
source: SABER-FISH uses OligoMiner to design 20–40 nt oligonucleotides (oligos) that are complementary to the RNA species of interest and are optimized for minimal off-target binding (Beliveau et al., 2018).
evidence: This describes the technical details of the SABER-FISH method, supported by citation.

claim: The oligos are pooled and extended using a Primer Exchange Reaction, which appends many copies of a short-repeated sequence (concatemers) to each oligo in the set.
source: The oligos are pooled and extended using a Primer Exchange Reaction (Kishi et al., 2018), which appends many copies of a short-repeated sequence (concatemers) to each oligo in the set.
evidence: This describes the technical details of probe set synthesis, supported by citation.

claim: The concatemers can be detected by the hybridization of fluorescent oligos.
source: The concatemers can then be detected by the hybridization of fluorescent oligos.
evidence: This describes the detection mechanism in SABER-FISH.

claim: Gene-specific probe sets against Vsx2 and Grik1 were designed for isolating specific BC subtypes.
source: We designed gene-specific probe sets against Vsx2, a marker of all BCs and MG, and Grik1, a marker of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 subtypes (~2% of all retinal cells) (Shekhar et al., 2016) (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is demonstrated by the experimental design and supported by citation to scRNA sequencing data.

claim: Vsx2 is a marker of all BCs and MG.
source: We designed gene-specific probe sets against Vsx2, a marker of all BCs and MG, and Grik1, a marker of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 subtypes (~2% of all retinal cells) (Shekhar et al., 2016) (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is established knowledge from scRNA sequencing studies, supported by citation.

claim: Grik1 is a marker of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 subtypes (~2% of all retinal cells).
source: We designed gene-specific probe sets against Vsx2, a marker of all BCs and MG, and Grik1, a marker of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 subtypes (~2% of all retinal cells) (Shekhar et al., 2016) (Figure 1b).
evidence: This is established knowledge from scRNA sequencing studies, supported by citation.

claim: 92.3 ± 0.6% of FACS-isolated Vsx2+ cells had Vsx2 puncta based on post-sort microscopy analysis.
source: To determine the purity of populations isolated using FACS, based on their SABER signal, the cells were placed on a microscope slide after FACS, and the percentage of cells that had Vsx2 puncta was quantified. This analysis showed 92.3 ± 0.6% had Vsx2 puncta, based on three individual sorts.
evidence: This is based on quantitative microscopy data from post-sort analysis.

claim: On average, 200,000 ± 0 Vsx2- cells, 96,000 ± 18,600 Grik1- cells, and 22,000 ± 1,000 Grik1+ cells were isolated per biological replicate from two retinas.
source: On average, we isolated 200,000 ± 0 Vsx2- cells, 96,000 ± 18,600 Grik1- cells, and 22,000 ± 1,000 Grik1+ cells per biological replicate, with each replicate originating from two retinas.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the cell sorting experiments.

claim: Gene-specific SABER-FISH can label dissociated cell populations for isolation by FACS.
source: These results indicate that gene-specific SABER-FISH can label dissociated cell populations for isolation by FACS.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful labeling and isolation experiments.

claim: Each sample was sequenced to a mean of 15 ± 3 million 75 bp paired-end reads.
source: Each sample was sequenced to a mean of 15 ± 3 million 75 bp paired-end reads to be able to reliably detect low abundance transcripts.
evidence: This is quantitative data about the sequencing depth.

claim: Gene body coverage of mapped reads indicated slight 3' bias, suggesting mild degradation of RNA, with a projected RNA Integrity Number (RIN) of approximately 4–6.
source: Gene body coverage of mapped reads indicated slight 3' bias, suggesting mild degradation of RNA, with a projected RNA Integrity Number (RIN) of approximately 4–6 (Sigurgeirsson et al., 2014).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the RNA-seq data, with citation to support the RIN estimation.

claim: Samples of the same cell population clustered together with an average Pearson correlation of r = 0.93.
source: Unbiased hierarchical clustering showed that samples of the same cell population clustered together (average Pearson correlation between samples within population: r = 0.93) (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of the RNA-seq data shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: Between Grik1- and Grik1+ populations, 1,740 genes were differentially expressed (adjusted p-value<0.05) out of 17,649 genes.
source: Between Grik1- and Grik1+ populations, we found 1,740 differentially expressed genes (adjusted p-value<0.05) out of 17,649 genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is quantitative data from differential expression analysis.

claim: The high number of genes detected indicates successful bulk RNA sequencing of low abundance transcripts.
source: The high number of genes detected indicates successful bulk RNA sequencing of low abundance transcripts.
evidence: This is an inference drawn from the large number of detected genes.

claim: The Vsx2- population was enriched for markers of all cell classes except for BCs and MG.
source: The Vsx2- population was enriched for markers of all cell classes except for BCs and MG (Figure 1—figure supplement 2), as expected from the expression pattern of Vsx2 (Shekhar et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis compared to known cell type markers, with citation.

claim: The Grik1- population was enriched for most BC and MG markers.
source: The Grik1- population was enriched for most BC and MG markers, while the Grik1+ population was enriched for a subset of BC markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis compared to known cell type markers.

claim: The Grik1+ population was enriched for a subset of BC markers.
source: The Grik1- population was enriched for most BC and MG markers, while the Grik1+ population was enriched for a subset of BC markers (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis compared to known cell type markers.

claim: Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) between Vsx2- and Grik1- populations indicated significant enrichment of rod, cone, AC, HC, and RGC markers in the Vsx2- populations and BC and MG markers in the Grik1- population.
source: Accordingly, Gene Set Enrichment Analysis (GSEA) between Vsx2- and Grik1- populations indicated significant enrichment of rod, cone, AC, HC, and RGC markers in the Vsx2- populations and BC and MG markers in the Grik1- population (default significance at FDR < 0.25; Enrichment in the Vsx2- population: Rod: FDR < 0.001; Cone: FDR < 0.001; AC: FDR < 0.001; HC: FDR = 0.174; RGC: FDR = 0.224; Enrichment in the Grik1- population: BC: FDR < 0.001; MG: FDR < 0.001).
evidence: This is based on GSEA statistical analysis of the RNA-seq data.

claim: The majority of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers were enriched in the Grik1+ population.
source: The majority of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers were enriched in the Grik1+ population as expected, and all other BC subtype markers were highly expressed in the Grik1- population (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis shown in Figure 1f.

claim: All other BC subtype markers were highly expressed in the Grik1- population.
source: The majority of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers were enriched in the Grik1+ population as expected, and all other BC subtype markers were highly expressed in the Grik1- population (Figure 1f).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis shown in Figure 1f.

claim: GSEA between Grik1- and Grik1+ populations confirmed enrichment of BC2, BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers in the Grik1+ population.
source: GSEA between Grik1- and Grik1+ populations confirmed these results (Enrichment in the Grik1+ population: BC2: FDR < 0.001; BC3A: FDR = 0.005; BC3B: FDR < 0.001; BC4: FDR < 0.001; Enrichment in the Grik1- population: BC1B: FDR = 0.132; BC5A: FDR = 0.135; BC5C: FDR = 0.136; BC5D: FDR = 0.172; BC6: FDR = 0.145; BC7: FDR = 0.169; BC8/9: FDR = 0.174; RBC: FDR < 0.001).
evidence: This is based on GSEA statistical analysis of the RNA-seq data.

claim: Tpbgl is a previously uncharacterized transcript that is expressed in Grik1+ cells.
source: The expression of Tpbgl, a previously uncharacterized transcript, was confirmed in Grik1+ cells by SABER-FISH in retinal tissue sections (Figure 1—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on FISH validation shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: The cell populations isolated and profiled by Probe-Seq correspond to the expected BC subtypes.
source: These results indicate that the cell populations isolated and profiled by Probe-Seq correspond to the expected BC subtypes.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the differential expression and GSEA analyses.

claim: 72% of GFP+ cells were Grik1+ using the Grik1CRM4-GFP reporter.
source: We previously showed that 72% of GFP+ cells were Grik1+ using this reporter (Kishi et al., 2019).
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: On average, 836 ± 155 GFP+ Live cells and 10,000 ± 0 Grik1+ Probe-Seq cells were collected for transcriptional analysis.
source: On average, 836 ± 155 GFP+ Live cells (n = 3) and 10,000 ± 0 Grik1+ Probe-Seq cells (n = 3) were collected for transcriptional analysis.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the cell sorting experiments.

claim: A slightly higher 3'−5' bias was observed for the RNA originating in the Probe-Seq population (1.02 ± 0.02) compared to the Live cell population (0.90 ± 0.01).
source: Based on the gene body coverage of the 10,000 most highly expressed genes, a slightly higher 3'−5' bias was observed for the RNA originating in the Probe-Seq population (1.02 ± 0.02) compared to the Live cell population (0.90 ± 0.01), indicating mild degradation of RNA with the Probe-Seq protocol.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of gene body coverage from RNA-seq data.

claim: The level of degradation for the Probe-Seq population would project to a RIN score of approximately 4–6.
source: Based on the gene body coverage graph, the level of degradation for the Probe-Seq population would project to a RIN score of approximately 4–6 (Sigurgeirsson et al., 2014) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is an inference based on gene body coverage analysis, with citation to support the RIN estimation.

claim: An analysis of expression levels of all genes between Live and Probe-Seq cells showed an average Pearson correlation of 0.78 ± 0.01.
source: An analysis of expression levels of all genes between Live and Probe-Seq cells showed an average Pearson correlation of 0.78 ± 0.01 (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is based on quantitative correlation analysis of RNA-seq data.

claim: When analyzing only the BC2 – BC4 subtype-specific markers, the average correlation was 0.66 between Live and Probe-Seq cells.
source: Notably, when analyzing only the (BC2 – BC4) subtype-specific markers, the average correlation was 0.66 between Live and Probe-Seq cells, with enrichment of these markers in the Probe-Seq population (Figure 1g).
evidence: This is based on quantitative correlation analysis of RNA-seq data for specific marker genes.

claim: The strong correlation between the transcriptomes obtained by Probe-Seq and traditional live cell sorting indicates that high quality transcriptomes of specific cell types can be obtained by this method.
source: Despite the imperfect match in the cellular compositions of these two preparations, the strong correlation between the transcriptomes obtained by Probe-Seq and traditional live cell sorting indicates that high quality transcriptomes of specific cell types can be obtained by this method.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the correlation analysis between Probe-Seq and live cell sorting.

claim: The ability to resolve a targeted cell population from the total cell population is predicted to be dependent upon the total number of fluorescent probes in that cell.
source: The ability to resolve a targeted cell population from the total cell population was predicted to be dependent upon the total number of fluorescent probes in that cell, which could be increased by targeting more oligos to each transcript, and/or by targeting more abundant RNA species.
evidence: This is a hypothesis about the factors affecting FACS resolution.

claim: Grik1, Grm6, and Neto1 exhibit high-to-low levels of gene expression based upon FISH analysis in retina tissue sections.
source: To investigate these parameters, three gene-specific probe sets were made for Grik1, Grm6, and Neto1, which exhibit high-to-low levels of gene expression based upon FISH analysis in retina tissue sections (Number of puncta per positive cell: Grik1: 37; Grm6: 20; Neto1: 6.5) (Figure 1—figure supplement 5).
evidence: This is based on quantitative FISH analysis shown in the supplementary figure.

claim: The Stain Index (SI) decreased with the reduced number of oligos and the level of expression of each gene.
source: The SI was found to decrease with the reduced number of oligos and the level of expression of each gene (Figure 1h).
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of FACS data with varying numbers of oligos.

claim: With an SI cutoff of 2, 12 oligos were sufficient for confidence in the separation of gene-positive and negative populations.
source: However, with an SI cutoff of 2, 12 oligos were sufficient for confidence in the separation of gene-positive and negative populations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the SI analysis with varying numbers of oligos.

claim: Neto1+ BCs constitute ~0.3% of all retinal cells.
source: Of note, Neto1+ BCs constitute ~0.3% of all retinal cells; nonetheless, a clear separation could be observed for this rare population.
evidence: This is based on known cell type frequencies and demonstrates the sensitivity of the method.

claim: Short transcripts, or few oligos can be used successfully to isolate rare cell types using Probe-Seq.
source: These results demonstrate that short transcripts, or few oligos can be used successfully to isolate rare cell types using Probe-Seq.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the experiments with varying numbers of oligos and rare cell types.

claim: Exchange-SABER has enabled the labeling of seven retinal cell classes using three cycles of FISH.
source: This allows fluorescent channels to be reused for detection of different genes in the same cells. Exchange-SABER has enabled the labeling of seven retinal cell classes using three cycles of FISH.
evidence: This is based on previous work with Exchange-SABER, representing established knowledge.

claim: Multiplexed Probe-Seq can allow detection of multiple cell types in the same cell preparation with one overnight hybridization of multiple gene-specific probe sets.
source: These results indicate that multiplexed Probe-Seq can allow detection of multiple cell types in the same cell preparation with one overnight hybridization of multiple gene-specific probe sets.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the iterative labeling and stripping experiments.

claim: The majority of mouse BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers were found to be enriched in the Grik1+ population from frozen mouse retina nuclei.
source: The majority of mouse BC3A, BC3B, and BC4 markers were found to be enriched in the Grik1+ population, as expected, and all other BC subtype markers were highly expressed in the Grik1- population (Figure 2—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis of nuclear RNA from frozen tissue.

claim: Cell type-specific nuclear RNA from frozen tissue can be isolated by Probe-Seq.
source: These results indicate that cell type-specific nuclear RNA from frozen tissue can be isolated by Probe-Seq.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful isolation and profiling of nuclei from frozen mouse retina.

claim: GRM6 is expressed in cone ON bipolar cells and rod bipolar cells (RBC) in the mouse and human retina.
source: Fresh-frozen human retinas (age range: 40–60; see Materials and methods for full description of samples) were then tested for isolation and profiling of human BC subtypes using a probe set for GRM6. This gene is expressed in cone ON bipolar cells and rod bipolar cells (RBC) in the mouse and human retina (Shekhar et al., 2016; Cowan et al., 2019) (Figure 2a).
evidence: This is established knowledge from scRNA sequencing studies, supported by citations.

claim: On average, 43,000 ± 35,500 GRM6- nuclei and 1,800 ± 781 GRM6+ nuclei were isolated from an approximately 5 mm x 5 mm square of the human retina per biological replicate.
source: On average, 43,000 ± 35,500 GRM- nuclei and 1,800 ± 781 GRM6+ nuclei were isolated from an approximately 5 mm x 5 mm square of the retina per biological replicate (Figure 2d).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the nuclear isolation experiments.

claim: Between GRM6- and GRM6+ populations from human retina, 1956 out of 9,619 genes were differentially expressed (adjusted p-value<0.05).
source: Upon filtering out genes with zero counts in more than four samples, 1956 out of 9,619 genes were differentially expressed (adjusted p-value<0.05).
evidence: This is quantitative data from differential expression analysis of human retina samples.

claim: An enrichment of markers for RBCs and ON BCs were found in the GRM6+ population from human retina.
source: An enrichment of markers for RBCs and ON BCs were found in the GRM6+ population (Figure 2e).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis compared to known cell type markers.

claim: GSEA between GRM6- and GRM6+ confirmed enrichment of RBC and ON BC markers in the GRM6+ population.
source: GSEA between GRM6- and GRM6+ confirmed these results (Enrichment in GRM6+ population: RBC: FDR = 0.003; ON BC-1: FDR = 0.181; ON BC-2: FDR = 0.126), indicating that the expected human retinal populations were accurately isolated.
evidence: This is based on GSEA statistical analysis of the RNA-seq data from human samples.

claim: CDH12 is a transcript highly enriched in the GRM6+ population.
source: The expression of CDH12, a transcript highly enriched in the GRM6+ population, but previously not reported to be a marker of these subtypes, was confirmed using SABER-FISH on fixed adult human retina sections (Figure 2f).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis and FISH validation.

claim: Nuclear transcripts isolated from frozen tissue by Probe-Seq are sufficient for transcriptional profiling.
source: These results show that nuclear transcripts isolated from frozen tissue by Probe-Seq are sufficient for transcriptional profiling.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful profiling of nuclei from frozen human retina.

claim: The adult Drosophila midgut is composed of four major cell types: enterocytes (EC), enteroendocrine cells (EE), enteroblasts (EB), and intestinal stem cells (ISC).
source: The adult Drosophila midgut is composed of four major cell types – enterocytes (EC), enteroendocrine cells (EE), enteroblasts (EB), and intestinal stem cells (ISC), though recent profiling studies have revealed heterogeneity among ECs and EEs (Dutta et al., 2015; Hung et al., 2018).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila gut anatomy, supported by citations.

claim: escargot (esg) is a well-characterized marker for ISCs and EBs.
source: We aimed to isolate ISCs and EBs using a gene-specific probe set for escargot (esg), a well-characterized marker for these cell types (Figure 3a).
evidence: This is established knowledge about Drosophila gut cell markers.

claim: On average, 1,400 ± 208 esg- cells and 1,000 ± 404 esg+ cells per biological replicate were isolated from Drosophila midguts.
source: On average, 1,400 ± 208 esg- cells and 1,000 ± 404 esg+ cells per biological replicate were isolated.
evidence: This is quantitative data from the cell sorting experiments on Drosophila gut.

claim: Between esg- and esg+ populations from Drosophila gut, 405 out of 1,596 genes were differentially expressed (adjusted p-value<0.05).
source: Upon filtering out genes with zero counts in more than three samples, 405 out of 1,596 genes were differentially expressed (adjusted p-value<0.05).
evidence: This is quantitative data from differential expression analysis of Drosophila samples.

claim: An enrichment of ISC/EB markers was observed in the esg+ population isolated using Probe-Seq from Drosophila gut.
source: An enrichment of ISC/EB markers was observed in the esg+ population isolated using Probe-Seq, while markers of all other cell types were enriched in the esg- population (Figure 3e).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis compared to known cell type markers.

claim: GSEA between esg+ and esg- populations isolated using Probe-Seq indicated significant enrichment of ISC/EB markers in the esg+ population and all other cell type markers in the esg- population.
source: GSEA between esg+ and esg- populations isolated using Probe-Seq indicated significant enrichment of ISC/EB markers in the esg+ population and all other cell type markers in the esg- population (Enrichment in esg+ population: ISC/EB: FDR < 0.001; Enrichment in esg- population: LFC: FDR < 0.001; aEC1: FDR < 0.001; aEC2: FDR < 0.001; aEC3: FDR < 0.001; pEC3: FDR < 0.001; AstA-EE: FDR < 0.001; mEC3: FDR < 0.001; Copper-Iron: FDR = 0.001; pEC2: FDR = 0.001; AstC: FDR = 0.004; aEC4: FDR = 0.003; pEC1: FDR = 0.004; dEC: FDR = 0.013; NPF-EE: FDR = 0.019).
evidence: This is based on GSEA statistical analysis of the RNA-seq data from Drosophila samples.

claim: Sox100B is a transcript significantly enriched in the esg+ population from Drosophila gut.
source: Using SABER-FISH on wholemounts of midguts, the co-localization of esg and Sox100B, a transcript significantly enriched in the esg+ population, was validated (Figure 3f).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis and FISH validation.

claim: Probe-Seq enables the isolation and transcriptional profiling of specific cell types from invertebrate tissue and from non-CNS tissue.
source: These results demonstrate that Probe-Seq enables the isolation and transcriptional profiling of specific cell types from invertebrate tissue and from non-CNS tissue.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful application to Drosophila gut.

claim: The central chicken retina contains a region thought to endow high acuity vision, given its cellular composition and arrangement of cells.
source: The central chicken retina contains a region thought to endow high acuity vision, given its cellular composition and arrangement of cells (da Silva and Cepko, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chick retina anatomy, supported by citation.

claim: The chick high acuity area is devoid of rod photoreceptors and enriched in cone photoreceptors, with a high density of RGCs.
source: It comprises a small and discrete area that is devoid of rod photoreceptors and enriched in cone photoreceptors, with a high density of RGCs, the output neurons of the retina (da Silva and Cepko, 2017; Bruhn and Cepko, 1996).
evidence: This is established knowledge about chick retina anatomy, supported by citations.

claim: FGF8, CYP26C1, and CYP26A1 are highly enriched in the chick high acuity area at embryonic day 6 (E6).
source: Although we have shown that FGF8, CYP26C1, and CYP26A1 are highly enriched in this area at embryonic day 6 (E6) (da Silva and Cepko, 2017), the other molecular determinants that may play a role in high acuity area development are unknown.
evidence: This is based on previous work by the authors, supported by citation.

claim: On average, 7,000 ± 6,950 FGF8+ cells and 189,000 ± 19,000 FGF8- cells were FACS isolated from HH28 chick retinas.
source: On average, 7,000 ± 6,950 FGF8+ cells and 189,000 ± 19,000 FGF8- cells were FACS isolated into individual populations (Figure 4c).
evidence: This is quantitative data from the cell sorting experiments on chick retina.

claim: Gene body coverage of mapped reads from chick retina showed more uniform distribution compared to that of adult mouse retina, suggesting reduced RNA degradation.
source: Interestingly, gene body coverage of mapped reads showed more uniform distribution compared to that of adult mouse retina, suggesting reduced RNA degradation. (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is based on analysis of RNA-seq data quality metrics.

claim: Between FGF8- and FGF8+ populations from chick retina, 1,924 DE genes out of 12,053 genes were found.
source: Between FGF8- and FGF8+ populations, we found 1,924 DE genes out of 12,053 genes.
evidence: This is quantitative data from differential expression analysis of chick samples.

claim: Among the top 50 most enriched DE transcripts in the FGF8+ population were FGF8, CYP1B1, and CYP26C1.
source: Among the top 50 most enriched DE transcripts in the FGF8+ population were FGF8, CYP1B1, and CYP26C1 (Figure 4d).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis of chick retina samples.

claim: CYP1B1 and CYP26C1 are components of the retinoic acid signaling pathway.
source: The latter two transcripts are components of the retinoic acid signaling pathway, and were previously shown to be highly enriched in the central retina where FGF8 is expressed (da Silva and Cepko, 2017).
evidence: This is established knowledge about these genes, supported by citation.

claim: DE analysis of the FGF8- and FGF8+ populations revealed enrichment of early differentiation markers of RGCs and photoreceptors in the FGF8- population, confirming that FGF8 is mostly expressed in central progenitor cells.
source: DE analysis of the FGF8- and FGF8+ populations revealed enrichment of early differentiation markers of RGCs (i.e. NEFL) and photoreceptors (i.e. NEUROD1) in the FGF8- population, confirming that FGF8 is mostly expressed in central progenitor cells (Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis and represents an inference about cell identity.

claim: BMP2 is a transcript enriched in the FGF8+ population in chick retina.
source: An additional SABER-FISH probe set for BMP2, a transcript enriched in the FGF8+ population, was then used on developing HH28 chick central retinal sections. BMP2 was found to be highly enriched within the FGF8+ population, that is, expression was confined to a discrete central retina where FGF8 was expressed (Figure 4e).
evidence: This is based on differential expression analysis and FISH validation.

claim: Probe-Seq of the developing chick retina using FGF8 as a molecular handle can reveal the transcriptional profile of the progenitor cells that will comprise the chick high acuity area.
source: These results indicate that Probe-Seq of the developing chick retina using FGF8 as a molecular handle can reveal the transcriptional profile of the progenitor cells that will comprise the chick high acuity area.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful profiling of FGF8+ cells in chick retina.

claim: Probe-Seq uses RNA for cell sorting rather than protein, making this method applicable across organisms.
source: Due to the reliance on RNA for cell sorting, rather than protein, this method is applicable across organisms.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful application to multiple organisms.

claim: Other RNA-based methods to label specific cell types for downstream sequencing have not been tested with tissue samples, and/or require cell encapsulation in a microfluidic device.
source: Other RNA-based methods to label specific cell types for downstream sequencing have not been tested with tissue samples, and/or require cell encapsulation in a microfluidic device (Klemm et al., 2014; Eastburn et al., 2014; Pellegrino et al., 2016).
evidence: This is based on citations to previous work and establishes the novelty of Probe-Seq.

claim: Aside from the different dissociation protocols, Probe-Seq does not require species- or tissue-specific alterations.
source: Aside from the different dissociation protocols, Probe-Seq does not require species- or tissue-specific alterations.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the successful application to multiple species and tissues.

claim: Multiplexed Probe-Seq allows for iterative labeling, sorting, and re-labeling with one overnight hybridization of multiple gene-specific probe sets.
source: To profile multiple cellular subtypes, multiplexed Probe-Seq allows for iterative labeling, sorting, and re-labeling with one overnight hybridization of multiple gene-specific probe sets.
evidence: This is demonstrated by the iterative labeling experiments.

claim: The Probe-Seq method is cost and time effective, with less than 6 hr of hands-on time, including FISH, FACS, and library preparation.
source: The Probe-Seq method is also cost and time effective, with less than 6 hr of hands-on time, including FISH, FACS, and library preparation.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience with the protocol.

claim: Excluding the wait time for oligo delivery, libraries ready for sequencing can be made by Probe-Seq in less than three days.
source: Excluding the wait time for oligo delivery, libraries ready for sequencing can be made by Probe-Seq in less than three days.
evidence: This is based on the authors' experience with the protocol.

claim: Per sample, the cost of Probe-Seq is estimated to be less than $200, from start to finish, achieving ~15 million paired-end reads.
source: Per sample, we estimate the cost to be less than $200, from start to finish, achieving ~15 million paired-end reads.
evidence: This is an estimate based on the authors' experience with the protocol.

claim: The Probe-Seq protocol may be further modified to use other single molecule FISH methods such as clampFISH or RNAscope rather than SABER-FISH.
source: For example, the protocol may be further modified to use other single molecule FISH methods such as clampFISH (Rouhanifard et al., 2019) or RNAscope (Wang et al., 2012) rather than SABER-FISH, as these methods have their respective strengths and weaknesses.
evidence: This is speculation about potential future modifications to the protocol, with citations to alternative methods.

claim: Adaptation of Probe-Seq for the reversal of crosslinks for scRNA sequencing will likely be necessary for further development.
source: Further development for scRNA sequencing after cell type enrichment using Probe-Seq may also be possible. For this, however, adaptation of Probe-Seq for the reversal of crosslinks for scRNA sequencing (Alles et al., 2017; Attar et al., 2018; Chen et al., 2018) will likely be necessary.
evidence: This is speculation about potential future developments, with citations to relevant methods.
